A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nAChRs of normal BECs are not only the target of the tobacco nitroso-compounds, but also the target of the anti-breast cancer agents, SLURP family proteins.

the tobacco nitrosamines, such as NNK, can activate nAChRs and induce the tumorigenic transformation in BECs, while SLURP- 1 can inhibit the nAChRs activation and abolish the tumorigenic effects induced by NNK in BECs.

the nicotinic signaling network of mamary epithelium can be targeted by the tobacco nitrosamines and their antagonists for the development of novel anti-breast therapies.
